evaluator_kind: AI model (independent of the rule engine edge_proposer.py that proposed the edges; not a human review)
criterion: ACCEPT only if the relation type (depends_on, part_of, related_to, supersedes, ...) is true for the content of both notes and the note content supports it; words in common without a link of meaning, wrong direction, wrong type and duplicate content are REJECT.
method: Per relation: the two notes' text was read from the working tree (frontmatter, body), plus the relation type and both quotes; where the notes cross-reference each other this was checked with grep. Nothing was tuned to a target precision.
limitations: Very large notes were read by frontmatter, opening section, heading outline and search for the quoted passage, not line by line: Master_Skills_Catalog_251 (~920k chars, #5), Regulament_UE_2016_679_GDPR (~438k, #21), Regulament_UE_2023_1114_MiCA (~769k, #22), Regulament_UE_2022_2554_DORA (~370k, #21), Ordinul_M172_2021 (~193k, #23), ELITE_QUANT_BOT_COMPLETE_PROMPT (~224k, #18-#20). Their verdicts rest on what the relation claims (type/direction) rather than on their full text.

Judgements about duplicates (#1, #2, #20, #47, #48, #49) reject edges between identical documents; if the owner accepts sibling-version edges as valid related_to, #49 (and arguably #47, #48) would flip.
A single evaluator. The 50 relations are a stratified sample (25 strong, 25 weak; seed 42), so per-stratum fractions are not estimates of the whole 'accepted' set with any known interval.

verdicts.rationale: Both notes are byte-for-byte the same auto-generated policy lesson (same error, cause, fix and rule, differing only by id). Identical content is a duplicate, not a dependency; nothing in either note says one relies on the other.
Same as #1: two identical policy-guard lessons. A `depends_on` between duplicates is meaningless; the shared tokens 'delete_canonical', 'high', 'risk' come from the template text.

Real topical overlap (SQLCipher/DPAPI encryption at rest), but the GDPR Art. 32 obligation note does not depend on a Perplexity-derived desktop PIN-auth pattern; at most the pattern implements the obligation. `depends_on` is false; `related_to` would be the honest type.

The source is derived from HG 585/2002 (art. 236-258, SIC accreditation) and never cites Ordin M172/2021. The target only shares the acronym ADS. The source quote is just the note's title. No dependency in either direction.

A generated 920k-character catalog of ~3,660 skills does not depend on the 21-agent matrix; the 'ast, aws, cdc, clickhouse, cqrs, dast' overlap is generic skill vocabulary. The quoted catalog row is not even the matrix's content. (Source read by head, outline and search, not line by line.)

Real link (CriticAgent / SelfRefine appear in both), but the procedure uses the agents, not the other way round: the architecture note does not depend on the reflexion procedure. Direction and type are wrong; `related_to` at best. The target quote is only a diagram node label.
A navigation index lists notes; an architecture note does not depend on the master index. The source quote is only its title and the shared words ('architecture', 'graph') are generic.

Legea 190/2018 is the Romanian act implementing the GDPR: its title says so and its 'Trimiteri' section names Regulation (UE) 2016/679. An implementing national law depends on the Regulation it implements, so `depends_on` is true and both quotes are on point.

The P1 context-packing lab is explicitly measured 'under the production baseline (P0)' and refines the P0 diagnostic (P0 found candidate discovery; P1 isolates packing failure). P1 builds on P0's pipeline and numbers, so `depends_on` holds; the two notes are consistent follow-ups on the same corpus.

HG 585/2002 (classified-information standards) does not depend on Legea-cadru 153/2017 (public-sector pay). The only link is that ORNISS is named in both; the salary bonus for ORNISS staff is irrelevant to the standards.

The two notes belong together, but the link is declared the other way: the trace protocol note already lists the audit-principles note as its target, and the principles do not cite the protocol. `depends_on` from principles to protocol reverses that.
A note on making the prompt-master skill portable across AI agents does not depend on a catalog of 130 MengTo web/3D skills; the overlap is the word 'skill' and 'elevenlabs'/'readme'.
prompt-master portability note vs the ui-sensei README: different skills, no reference either way; overlap is 'skill', 'MIT', 'provenance'.
An ADR about REVIEW->ACTIVE lifecycle transitions does not depend on the FinScope app note; FinScope only mentions MemoryController and the invariants in boilerplate.
The P5 search-integration report has no dependency on the FinScope project note; the match is the boilerplate sentence about MemoryController invariants in FinScope.

The P5 report is the delivery of the retrieval-integration item that the runtime-security gaps note lists as remaining ('Retrieval production integration remains deferred to Antigravity') and it is stated against the same security head (PR #17). So P5 depends on that security closure. Caveat: the quoted target sentence (lifecycle routing) is not the evidence; the notes' own content is.

The original request (upgrade the vault into a self-improving cognitive brain) and the protocol for building programs with a 14-agent council do not depend on each other; overlap is generic vocabulary (OODA, SelfRefine, WAL, SHA-256). The target quote is an agent table unrelated to the source quote.

The audit examines the v1 snapshot of the trading bot against the architect system prompt; it never cites the 217k-character reconstruction prompt copy in cerebras-agent, which describes a different version of the code. Shared tokens are function names ('_evaluate_and_trade', 'auditlogger'). (Target read by head, outline and search, not line by line.)

The complete-reconstruction prompt and the V10 application README describe the same trading bot (both cover the MT5 filling-mode bitmask, DEAL_ENTRY_OUT PnL, 300+ strategy instances), but neither depends on the other, and the tie to V10 specifically is unsupported: the V11 application note is identical apart from the version label. Same-application documentation, not a dependency.

Same target and same reasoning as #19; the source is just the copy of the prompt file under cerebras-agent/ (the two source files are the same document), so this proposal is a duplicate of #19 and fails for the same reason.

DORA (digital operational resilience of finance) does not replace the GDPR; both regulations are in force side by side. A `supersedes` edge requires one act repealing or replacing the other, and the overlap here is boilerplate ('Regulamentul', 'Parlamentului', 'DPO'). The quotes are just the two titles. (Both regulations are 370-440k characters; read by head, outline and search.)

MiCA (crypto-assets) does not supersede the structured index of DORA, and the source is a legal-source note while the target is an analytical index. The quotes are governance disclaimers common to every legal note; 'EIOPA', 'ESMA', 'TIC' is shared regulatory vocabulary.

The index of Ordin M172/2021 is derived from the order and summarises it; the order does not supersede its own index. If anything the relation is derived_from/indexed_by. The quotes (a NATO norms reference and a definition of CDC) merely share terms.

The hypothesis registry tracks testable hypotheses (its R-H005 concerns candidate generation as the primary bottleneck, the P0 finding); it does not replace the P0 findings note, which stays the measurement that the registry cites. Related, not superseding. Both quotes are only titles.

A semantic-mesh architecture note (object taxonomy, relation model) does not supersede the multi-agent execution protocol (source-of-truth rules, delegation model); they cover different subjects and the overlap is generic ('agent', 'evidence', 'procedure').

The general Security Practices note lists 'GPO baseline' as one of its domains; the GPO Baseline Deployment project is therefore (loosely) a part of that topic, not the reverse. `part_of` from the practices note to the project inverts it, and neither note cites the other. The source is a generic reference, the target a specific project with a known `$PSScriptRoot` issue.

The note is the deployment and operation SOP for the XAU_Kinetic engine, and the target project note 'Elite Quant Bot / XAU_Kinetic' links to it ([[Deploy_XAU_Kinetic_Quant_Bot]]) and covers the same components (xau_kinetic, config, SHA-256 audit log, MT5). A deployment procedure is part of that project's documentation, so `part_of` is true.

An order of the Ministry of Defence on classified information is a legal norm; it is not a component of the Registru Transferuri application specification, whose 'Conformitate Normativă' line does not even list M172/2021 (it lists HG 585/2002, Legea 182/2002, NATO, EU, NIST, IEEE). The overlap is domain vocabulary (INFOSEC, NATO, storage media).

The multi-agent execution protocol (source-of-truth and delegation rules) is not part of a procedure for configuring a Perplexity Space for the Registru project; the only link is the word 'Perplexity' appearing in the protocol's delegation list.

SLOT_DECISIONS is a separate decision document that the reconciliation report cites as an authority ('Governed by ... SLOT_DECISIONS.md'); it is not a part of the report. The relation is references/supports, not part_of. The quotes are just the two titles.

The Desktop Application description (Registru Militar de Transferuri & Device Control v5.4: WPF .NET 10, air-gapped, SQLite/SQLCipher, HG 585/2002, NATO, EUCI, NIST) is the product documentation of the project that the Registru de Transferuri note describes with the same stack and normative list. Being part of that project's documentation set is true. Caveat: the two notes differ on details (PIN hashing), and a near-identical copy exists as the Workspace Specification (see #33, #47).

A trading-journal SaaS (journal, broker import, AI coach, Romanian tax module) is not a part of the 4-agent Gemini coding team; the overlap is trading vocabulary ('RSI', 'MACD', 'JWT', 'USDT') and the quotes describe two unrelated products.

Same reasoning as #31: the Workspace Specification (Registru Militar de Transferuri & Device Control v5.4) is the specification of the application that the Registru de Transferuri project note describes with the same stack, air-gapped scope and normative list, so it is part of that project's documentation. Caveat: near-duplicate of the Desktop Application note (see #31, #47) and it differs from the project note on details.

02_map and 05_state are two sibling slots of the same 16-slot ontology (different questions: 'where does information live' vs 'what is real now'); neither is part of the other. The overlap is the identical table header and book names that occur in every slot file. Both quotes are candidate-concept table rows from different concepts.

ONTOLOGY_SPEC defines the ontology and its 16 canonical slots; its slot table has the consolidation row with the same question ('How does experience become knowledge?'), the same sources (McClelland et al. 1995, Kumaran & Hassabis 2016) and the same validated modules as 16_consolidation.md. A slot file is a member of the ontology the spec defines, so `part_of` is true.

Both notes cover the same installation, PaperCut MF Secure Access on Xerox VersaLink via EIP 3.7 (CWIS access, ports, card/PIN release). The target is the reference resource for the source's setup and lists the source under 'Related'. `related_to` is true and the two titles say it.

The PIN-auth + SQLCipher/DPAPI pattern is the security design for air-gapped desktop apps that must comply with HG 585/2002 and the MS 111/172/191 rules; the source's own frontmatter lists [[HG585_MS111_Compliance_Requirements]] as related and the target covers the same air-gapped transfer-register context. A `related_to` edge is true; a stronger type would not be.

The PIN-auth + encrypted-storage pattern is the security design that the Registru de Transferuri evolved through (its 'Examples' section names that project and the v3.x PIN/SQLCipher/DPAPI steps), and SECURITY.md is that project's security model (air-gapped, DPAPI-protected SQLite WAL, hardened authentication). Same system, same controls: `related_to` is true. The two differ on detail (PIN hashing scheme), so nothing stronger is claimed.

Same engine (XAU_Kinetic): the procedure describes how to deploy and operate it, the architecture note explains its layers (domain, application, infrastructure, risk, strategies, SHA-256 audit persistence). The project note links both. `related_to` is accurate.

Both concern the Registru Militar de Transferuri WPF app: the standards note fixes the rules (ObsidianTactical.xaml, full ControlTemplates for ScrollBar/ComboBox/TextBox/DataGrid, MVVM, air-gapped sidecar) and the /remodelUI workflow executes the UI tasks that implement them (Sarcina 2 asks for exactly those ControlTemplates). `related_to` is true.

The multi-agent contracts note defines the roles of Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity and the Perplexity Space (section 'Perplexity Space - Rol de Research') for the Registru project; the target is the procedure that sets up that Perplexity Space. Same project, same role definition: `related_to` is accurate.

The 21-agent matrix states that the agents are 'conectati la skill registry', and the 50,000+ skills index is that registry's master index (same category, both ACTIVE/verified in the council/orchestration set). The link is real, though the shared tokens ('aws', 'gcp', 'llm', 'mcp') are generic and the quoted rows alone would not show it.

The benchmarks guide defines LoCoMo, LongMemEval and the retrieval metrics (MRR etc.); the remediation to-do's Phase 3 'Evaluare empirica' plans a LoCoMo smoke test and reports P@5, R@5, MRR. The plan is the place where those benchmarks/metrics are to be used, so `related_to` is true, though loosely: the to-do does not cite the guide.

ONTOLOGY_SPEC is the specification of the 16 slots and the Judgement slot file is one of them (its frontmatter follows the spec's schema). `related_to` is true, though a stronger 'defined by' type would be more exact.

The coordination specification's cold-start list names UNIVERSAL_AGENT_MEMORY_PROTOCOL_V1.md as the first file to read and both cover the same agents (CODEX, ANTIGRAVITY, PERPLEXITY, LUNA) and the same CURRENT.md continuity mechanism. Explicit cross-reference: `related_to` is true.

The bootstrap file's step 2 tells every agent to read UNIVERSAL_AGENT_MEMORY_PROTOCOL_V1.md and repeats its CURRENT.md/SHA rules; the protocol is the policy the bootstrap operationalises. An explicit citation plus the same subject makes `related_to` true.

The two notes have byte-identical bodies (a diff shows only the title and type lines of the frontmatter differ): they are one document stored twice. A `related_to` edge between copies carries no information; the correct handling is de-duplication, and the edge would only make retrieval return the same text twice.

The two notes have identical bodies (the diff shows only the title line differs): one 'Trading Bot v2.0' README stored in two project folders. A `related_to` between copies conveys nothing; it needs de-duplication, not an edge. Both quotes are the same passage.

The V10 and V11 application notes are identical apart from the version label in the title (checked by diffing with the label normalised). They are real sibling versions of one bot, but the notes give no content from which a relation could be read, and the quotes are the same 'Requirements' block. Judged with the other duplicate pairs (#47, #48); if the owner counts sibling versions as a valid `related_to`, this flips to ACCEPT.

Both are ACTIVE procedures about the same system: the first specifies the bio-inspired cognitive modules of AI Memory Vault (ACT-R activation, reconsolidation, cognitive_core), the second the blueprint for integrating that system into a large application, whose sidecar example imports cognitive_core. Architecture and its integration guide are related. Weak link: the quoted ACT-R formula and the code snippet do not show it; the notes' subject matter does.
